deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics. It is not a working page by Riemann. It is the draft of the editors' introduction (by Dedekind and/or H. Weber, editors of the Gesammelte Werke, 1876) to the section 'Fragmente philosophischen Inhalts', and it is written in an editor's hand with editorial deletions and insertions. Its content, in order:

(a) Editorial preamble.
- Riemann's philosophical speculations occupied him for a large part of his life.
- The dates of the individual essays are hard to establish.
- The surviving fragments are far from a coherent treatment prepared for publication, though some passages suggest Riemann at times intended one.
- The fragments do suffice to characterise his standpoint on psychological and natural-philosophical questions and to indicate the course of his investigations. Detailed execution is almost entirely missing.

(b) A quoted self-description by Riemann of 'the works which now chiefly occupy me':
1. To introduce the imaginary (complex-variable methods) into the theory of further transcendental functions. This follows the successful treatment of algebraic, exponential/circular, elliptic and Abelian functions. He says the necessary groundwork is in his Inaugural Dissertation, Art. 20.
2. Connected new methods for integrating partial differential equations, already applied successfully to several physical problems.
3. His 'main work': a new conception of the known laws of nature, expressed through other fundamental concepts. This would allow experimental data on the interaction of heat, light, magnetism and electricity to be used to investigate their connection. He was led to this chiefly by Newton, Euler and Herbart. He accepts Herbart's earliest results, those of the Promotions- and Habilitationsthesen of 22/23 October 1802. He departs from Herbart's later speculation in one essential point, which affects natural philosophy and the parts of psychology connecting to it.

(c) A second quoted note: 'The author is a Herbartian in psychology and epistemology (methodology and eidolology), but mostly cannot follow Herbart's natural philosophy and the related metaphysical disciplines (ontology and synechology).'

The previous page is an excerpt from Herbart (W. V. p. 446) on the serial association of representations. It was evidently copied as source material for the same philosophical section.

There is no derivation to restate. The text corresponds closely to the editors' introduction to the philosophical fragments printed in Riemann's Gesammelte mathematische Werke.
errors: No mathematical errors; there is no mathematics on the page.
Historical claims check out: Riemann's dissertation (1851) Art. 20 is where he announces applying his methods to other transcendental functions. Herbart's Göttingen theses do date from October 1802.

results.what: Riemann's self-description of his research programme: complex-function methods for further transcendental functions, new PDE integration methods, and a unified field-theoretic reformulation of physical laws (heat, light, magnetism, electricity), inspired by Newton, Euler and Herbart.
results.modern_name: Riemann's research programme / Naturphilosophie (unified physics, ether theory)
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (published posthumously by Dedekind & Weber, Gesammelte Werke 1876, 'Fragmente philosophischen Inhalts')

deep.surprise_reason: This is the editors' draft introduction to a section of Riemann's published Werke. It quotes Riemann notes that have been in print since 1876 and are widely discussed in the literature on Riemann and Herbart. There is no mathematics and nothing new.
transcription_corrections: The hand and content indicate this is the editors' (Dedekind/Weber) draft introduction, not a Riemann autograph.

'Die vorhandenen Fragmente sind meist entweder nur einer zusammenhängenden, zu publicirenden ... Bearbeitung' probably reads 'sind weit entfernt von einer zusammenhängenden, zur Publication bestimmten (corrected: bereiteten) Bearbeitung'.

'sie genügen ebenfalls kaum, den Standpunkt' should probably be 'sie genügen jedenfalls (aber), den Standpunkt'. 'kaum' contradicts the following 'leider aber fehlt fast jede Ausführung im Einzelnen'.
The deleted words at the start of line 1 ('aus dem [-...-] Nachlass') appear to be a struck-out adjective such as 'hinterlassenen' or 'handschriftlichen'; it is illegible.
'Riemann' appears as an insertion over a deleted word; '{+haben+}' is inserted above, and '[-zu haben-]' is deleted after 'beschäftigt'.
The struck word before 'An einer andern Stelle' is likely 'Ferner' or a similar connective.
The mark '4k' at the lower right is an archival or sheet mark, not text.
